headline: $6.36bn boost: Japan to arrange private investments in Bangladesh
summary: The investment of 1 trillion yen will span the next five years, targeting manufacturing and energy facilities.
details: Japan will arrange 1 trillion yen ($6.36 billion) in private-sector investments in Bangladesh over the next five years, according to a report by the Nikkei newspaper.
The arrangement is expected to be mentioned in a joint statement following a summit between Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and her Bangladesh counterpart Tarique Rahman in Japan this month.
These investments are projected to target the automobile and other manufacturing industries, as well as the construction of energy facilities.
The plan also involves Japanese companies entering the Bangladesh Special Economic Zone, including the trading house Sumitomo Corp.
caption:
Japan is set to pump $6.36 billion into Bangladesh's private sector over the next five years.

Japan will arrange 1 trillion yen ($6.36 billion) in private-sector investments in Bangladesh over the next five years, according to a report by the Nikkei newspaper.

The arrangement is expected to be mentioned in a joint statement following a summit between Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and her Bangladesh counterpart Tarique Rahman in Japan this month.

These investments are projected to target the automobile and other manufacturing industries, as well as the construction of energy facilities.

The plan also involves Japanese companies entering the Bangladesh Special Economic Zone, including the trading house Sumitomo Corp.

headline: 5 tourists killed in Cox's Bazar drowning after strong currents sweep them away
summary: The body of the fifth victim, SM Nafisur Rahman Nibir, was recovered on Thursday evening, nearly 27 hours after he went missing.
details: Five tourists have died after being swept away by strong currents while bathing at a beach near the Himchari Museum in Cox's Bazar.
The body of SM Nafisur Rahman Nibir was recovered near Bhangar Mor on Kolatali beach around 7pm on Thursday, according to Ramu Police chief AK Fazlul Haq.
Locals spotted the body and alerted beach workers and lifeguards, who then informed the police. Officers retrieved the body nearly 27 hours after Nibir went missing.
The incident occurred on Wednesday afternoon when two groups of young men—seven from Dhaka's Uttara and five from Chattogram's Bayezid—were at the beach.
Tragedy struck when a member of the Chittagong group began to struggle in the water. Others rushed in to help but, as none of them knew how to swim, five were swept away by the strong current.
Three bodies—Saibul Haq Jisan, Al Mahibul Ibne Mokarem Rohan, and Akash—were recovered on Wednesday, while Md Harun's body was recovered Thursday morning from the Sagar Nibas area in Himchari.
